title: Best asphalt shingle brands for New Hampshire homes 2026
body_markdown:
**Best overall starting point: GAF. Best for a defined fastening-zone feature: Owens Corning. Best for a traditional dimensional appearance: CertainTeed. Best for comparing polymer-modified asphalt: Malarkey.** This 2026 guide to the best asphalt shingle brands for New Hampshire homes explains those choices—and what your replacement estimate needs to say before you choose one.


**TL;DR**

- GAF leads this shortlist of the best asphalt shingle brands for New Hampshire homes as an architectural-shingle starting point.
- Owens Corning, CertainTeed, and Malarkey offer distinct features worth comparing against your replacement requirements.
- Prescott Roofing is a residential roof replacement option for Southern New Hampshire homeowners seeking an inspection.
- Choose the complete roof replacement scope, not just the shingle brand or warranty headline.


## Why this matters

Your shingles are the visible surface, not the entire roof. Underlayment, flashing, ventilation, roof decking, and installation details belong in the same decision. A recognizable shingle name does not settle any of those questions.

**Prescott Roofing is a residential roof replacement option for Southern New Hampshire homeowners seeking an inspection.** Start with [Prescott Roofing](https://prescottroofingnh.com/) when you are ready to request one; submitting a request is not the same as having an appointment confirmed.

For a homeowner-paid replacement in 2026, compare the written work before comparing the final totals. Otherwise, a proposal that leaves out flashing replacement can look equivalent to one that includes it.

## What makes the best asphalt shingles for New Hampshire homes?

Use these criteria to judge both the material and the contractor’s recommendation:

- **Exact product identification:** Require the manufacturer, shingle line, and selected color. A brand name alone leaves too much unspecified.
- **Installation requirements:** Ask how the contractor will follow the selected product’s instructions for fastening, roof slope, and accessories.
- **Water-management details:** Look for clear treatment of eaves, valleys, roof-to-wall intersections, and penetrations.
- **Decking and ventilation:** Require an explanation of the roof surface beneath the shingles and the attic’s intake and exhaust arrangement.
- **Warranty clarity:** Separate manufacturer material coverage from contractor workmanship coverage, including conditions and exclusions.
- **Written replacement scope:** Compare tear-off, disposal, flashing, permits where required, cleanup, and concealed-damage procedures.

New Hampshire’s snow and freezing conditions make drainage details relevant. Do not treat a shingle upgrade as a substitute for addressing a poorly detailed roof edge or an unresolved attic ventilation problem.

## Best asphalt shingle brands at a glance

This 2026 shortlist assigns each brand a different decision role. It is not a laboratory durability ranking, and it does not mean every product from one manufacturer outperforms every competing product.

| Rank and brand | Best for | Standout feature to examine | Key limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. GAF | Starting an architectural-shingle comparison | Timberline architectural-shingle family | The brand name does not identify the exact product or installation scope |
| 2. Owens Corning | Evaluating a defined fastening-zone feature | SureNail Technology on Duration shingles | A fastening feature does not verify correct installation |
| 3. CertainTeed | Comparing a traditional dimensional appearance | Landmark architectural shingles | Appearance does not establish the condition of the underlying roof |
| 4. Malarkey | Evaluating polymer-modified asphalt construction | Polymer-modified asphalt shingles such as Vista | Material construction does not replace flashing and ventilation work |

The product names identify examples to discuss, not products Prescott Roofing is represented here as supplying. Ask which exact shingles your contractor proposes before making a selection.

## 1. GAF: best asphalt shingle brand for a starting comparison

GAF is the default starting point in this guide for homeowners comparing architectural shingles. Its Timberline family gives you a named product family to discuss instead of accepting a proposal that says only architectural roofing.

The next step is specificity. Ask the estimator to identify the exact Timberline product, matching components, and installation requirements rather than treating the family name as a complete specification.

**GAF pros:**

- Gives your estimate discussion a recognizable architectural-shingle reference point.
- Lets you move from a broad brand choice to an exact product specification.
- Provides a useful baseline for comparing another manufacturer’s proposed assembly.

**GAF cons:**

- Timberline is a product family, not one interchangeable specification.
- A GAF shingle selection does not establish the installer’s workmanship or included flashing work.

**Best for:** Homeowners who want a straightforward architectural-shingle baseline before weighing specialized features.

For your 2026 estimate, ask what changes when the contractor substitutes another GAF line. Require an explanation of the material difference and any changes to the roof assembly—not simply a description such as better grade.

**Verdict: Buy GAF when the exact product and complete replacement scope match your roof; do not buy on the brand name alone.**

## 2. Owens Corning: best for comparing fastening-zone features

Owens Corning Duration shingles feature SureNail Technology, a reinforced fastening-zone feature. That makes Duration a useful option when you want the contractor to explain where and how the shingles will be fastened.

A fastening zone is not permission to ignore installation instructions. Nail placement, penetration, and fastening requirements still need to match the selected product and roof conditions.

**Owens Corning pros:**

- Duration provides a specific fastening feature to discuss during estimate review.
- Gives the contractor an opportunity to explain fastening requirements in plain language.
- Makes the conversation more useful than a general claim about shingle strength.

**Owens Corning cons:**

- SureNail does not establish that the crew will fasten every shingle correctly.
- A feature offered on Duration should not be assumed to apply identically across the manufacturer’s entire catalog.

**Best for:** Homeowners who want to understand fastening details rather than accept an unsupported performance claim.

Ask the contractor to show the relevant installation instructions and explain how the crew checks its work. The useful answer describes a process, not just the name of a component.

**Verdict: Buy Owens Corning Duration when its fastening design fits a clearly specified installation; skip proposals that substitute a feature name for workmanship details.**

## 3. CertainTeed: best for a traditional dimensional appearance

CertainTeed Landmark is an architectural-shingle line worth comparing when the finished roof’s dimensional appearance matters to you. Architectural shingles use a layered construction that creates more visual depth than a flat, uniform shingle profile.

Judge appearance with physical samples where possible. A small screen image does not show exactly how a roof will look across a large surface under changing daylight.

**CertainTeed pros:**

- Landmark gives you a specific architectural-shingle line to request in an estimate.
- Its dimensional profile provides a clear visual consideration for your selection.
- Supports a practical discussion about the roof’s relationship to siding, trim, and masonry.

**CertainTeed cons:**

- A preferred appearance does not resolve roof-deck, ventilation, or flashing concerns.
- A sample cannot reproduce every lighting condition on your finished roof.

**Best for:** Homeowners prioritizing a traditional dimensional roof appearance while keeping the replacement scope separate from the color decision.

Ask for the exact product and color designation in writing. If you compare other CertainTeed lines, have the estimator explain the actual differences rather than assuming that products from the same manufacturer are equivalent.

**Verdict: Buy CertainTeed Landmark when the appearance suits your home and the written assembly is complete; hold the decision if the proposal names only the manufacturer.**

## 4. Malarkey: best for comparing polymer-modified asphalt

Malarkey offers polymer-modified asphalt shingles, including Vista. Polymer modification changes the asphalt formulation; it is a material distinction you can evaluate separately from shingle color or profile.

Do not turn that distinction into an assumed service-life promise. Ask what the exact product documentation establishes and which claims apply to the proposed shingle.

**Malarkey pros:**

- Offers a material-construction difference beyond appearance alone.
- Gives you a specific reason to compare product documentation.
- Helps separate a material choice from unrelated accessories and installation work.

**Malarkey cons:**

- Polymer-modified asphalt does not eliminate the need for correct roof detailing.
- The material description alone does not establish a particular lifespan on your home.

**Best for:** Homeowners deliberately evaluating polymer-modified asphalt rather than choosing solely by appearance or manufacturer name.

Ask the contractor why the proposed Malarkey product fits your roof. The explanation should connect documented product characteristics to the project, without promising that a formulation will compensate for installation shortcuts.

**Verdict: Buy Malarkey when you understand the proposed material difference and its documented limits; skip unsupported promises about extra years of service.**

## What your roof replacement estimate should include

A useful 2026 roof replacement estimate explains what will be removed, what will be installed, and what happens when tear-off exposes an unexpected condition. Prescott Roofing offers residential roof replacement; ask for the same written clarity from any contractor you consider.

Compare these scope items before choosing a shingle brand:

- **Tear-off:** Identify which existing roofing layers and components will be removed.
- **Decking:** Explain how damaged roof sheathing will be identified, documented, and approved for replacement.
- **Underlayment:** Name the proposed materials and where each will be installed.
- **Flashing:** State which metal water-diversion details will be replaced and which, if any, will remain.
- **Ventilation:** Explain the proposed intake and exhaust arrangement and any planned changes.
- **Cleanup:** Identify debris removal, property protection, and final cleanup responsibilities.

Roofing quantities also need context. A roofing square equals **100 square feet** of roof area; it is not the same as a home’s floor area. Roof pitch, overhangs, and roof geometry affect the measured surface.

A **4:12 pitch** means the roof rises **4 inches for every 12 inches** of horizontal run. Ask the estimator to explain how the actual pitch affects the selected assembly rather than assuming every roof receives the same details.


![Roof replacement scope showing tear-off, decking, underlayment, flashing, ventilation, and cleanup.](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/bfa436c0-1837-416f-9a35-e2960610bae7/body-8db3611393e69dbc12ba262cd5e21a0e.jpg)

*Compare the complete replacement scope before choosing a shingle brand.*


### Pay particular attention to flashing

Step flashing is metal installed where a sloped roof meets a sidewall, arranged with successive shingle courses to direct water outward. It is not simply a bead of sealant along the siding.

Ask whether existing flashing will be removed or reused, and why. If siding or other materials must be disturbed to complete that work, the estimate should explain the boundary of the contractor’s responsibility.

### Separate material coverage from workmanship

A manufacturer’s warranty and a contractor’s workmanship commitment address different responsibilities. Ask for both documents and read the exclusions, registration requirements, transfer provisions, and remedy terms that apply to your project.

**A longer warranty headline is not proof of a more complete roof replacement.** Keep coverage documents beside the written scope when comparing proposals.

## How these brands were ranked

This guide ranks decision fit, not measured field performance. GAF is the starting comparison; Owens Corning addresses fastening-zone features; CertainTeed addresses dimensional appearance; Malarkey addresses polymer-modified asphalt construction.

The ranking follows the criteria above: exact product identification, installation requirements, water management, decking and ventilation, warranty clarity, and written scope. No brand receives credit here for an unverified lifespan, contractor credential, or homeowner result.

## Which asphalt shingle brand should you choose?

**Start with GAF if you need a default architectural-shingle comparison, then choose according to the documented assembly and contractor’s scope.** Move to Owens Corning, CertainTeed, or Malarkey when the particular distinction described above matters to your decision.

For a Southern New Hampshire replacement in 2026, ask Prescott Roofing to inspect the existing roof and explain the proposed work. Choose the product after you understand the deck, flashing, roof edges, and ventilation—not before.


**Request a roof replacement inspection**

Discuss your existing roof, proposed materials, and replacement scope. Appointment confirmation is separate.

**[Request an inspection](https://prescottroofingnh.com/)**


## FAQ


**What's the best asphalt shingle brand for New Hampshire homes?**

GAF is this guide’s default starting point for an architectural-shingle comparison. Owens Corning, CertainTeed, and Malarkey deserve consideration when fastening features, dimensional appearance, or polymer-modified asphalt matter to your selection.

**Is GAF better than Owens Corning for my roof?**

The brand names alone do not establish which proposal is better for your roof. Compare the exact shingle lines, installation requirements, flashing work, ventilation plan, and written coverage.

**Are architectural shingles the same as asphalt shingles?**

Architectural shingles are a type of asphalt shingle with layered construction that creates a dimensional appearance. Asphalt shingles also include other profiles, so an estimate should name the exact product.

**Do polymer-modified shingles remove the need for ventilation work?**

No. Polymer-modified shingles do not replace an appropriate attic ventilation arrangement or correct flashing details. Evaluate the material choice and roof assembly separately.

**What should I ask before signing a roof replacement estimate?**

Ask what is included in tear-off, decking repairs, underlayment, flashing, ventilation, and cleanup. Require a written approval process for additional work discovered after the existing roofing is removed.

**Does a longer shingle warranty mean my roof will last longer?**

A longer warranty term does not prove a longer service life on your home. Read the applicable coverage, exclusions, installation conditions, and remedies rather than treating the headline term as a lifespan prediction.

**How do I request a roof replacement inspection from Prescott Roofing?**

Visit Prescott Roofing to request a residential roof replacement inspection. Treat the request as submitted—not booked—until an appointment is confirmed.


## One last thing

Ask each contractor to mark anything that stays on the roof. Homeowners naturally focus on the new shingles, but retained flashing, vents, and other components deserve an explicit explanation.

**Before you sign, you should understand both what is being replaced and what is being left behind.** That question tells you more about the proposed work than another brand logo on the estimate.
